title: Near-Surface Temperature (GEOS-FP)
source: NASA GMAO GEOS-FP model, NASA Scientific Visualization Studio (SVS 5147)
description: A flat map of the whole Earth showing the air temperature 2 meters above the ground, hour by hour from 30 October to 14 November 2026, from NASA's GEOS-FP weather model. Colors run from dark blue, white and purple (-40 C) through blue, cyan, yellow, orange and red to dark red and grey (+40 C). The tropics stay warm and steady, deserts heat up every afternoon, and the Arctic, Siberia and northern Canada get colder as winter arrives.
listening_guide: Five held voices, one for each band of latitude, from the Arctic to Antarctica. Warmer = higher. Each step up or down is about 1 degree C.
Listen to the Arctic voice sink as winter sets in, and the Antarctic voice rise with the southern spring.
Plucks = places hotter than 30 C. Hotter = higher and louder.
Every day the plucks sweep from right to left: afternoon heat moves west with the sun, from Asia to Africa to the Americas.
Wind = how much of the Northern Hemisphere is below freezing. It grows as winter comes.
A chime rings at the start of every day (midnight UTC).

title: Global Rain and Snow (IMERG)
source: NASA GPM IMERG precipitation, NASA Scientific Visualization Studio
description: A flat map of the whole Earth, showing a week of rain and snow measured by NASA's Global Precipitation Measurement satellites (IMERG), in half-hour steps. Rain is drawn in green, yellow and red (light to heavy); snow in light blue to purple. Rain bands sweep across the oceans from west to east, a belt of storms circles the tropics, and snow falls mostly near the poles.
listening_guide: Raindrops: each pluck is rain somewhere on Earth. More drops = more rain.
Left to right in your headphones = west to east on the map.
Higher drops = rain further north, lower drops = further south.
Low rumble and booms = heavy downpours (10 mm per hour or more).
The warm chord swells as rain spreads and fades as it shrinks; it changes and a chime rings at the start of every day.
